# Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University

> A Harvard-based research center translating early childhood development science into actionable policy and practice through evidence-based frameworks and strategic partnerships.

The Center on the Developing Child conducts and synthesizes research on how early experiences shape lifelong health and development. It bridges the gap between scientific discovery and policy implementation through strategic communications, scientific councils, and collaborative partnerships focused on equity and systemic change.

## Key Topics

- Early Childhood Development
- Brain Architecture
- Serve and Return
- Toxic Stress
- Developmental Environments
- Child Development Science
- Policy Impact
- Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
- Science Communication
- Critical Periods
- Lifelong Health and Well-being
- Responsive Caregiving
- Scientific Councils
- FrameWorks Institute
- EASEL Lab

## Core Mission and Approach

- [Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University](https://developingchild.harvard.edu): Homepage introducing Center's mission on child development science and key concepts.
- [Our Approach - How to Make Science Actionable for Policymakers](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/our-approach): Center's four core strategies for translating science into policy action.
- [Strategic Science Communications for Effective Policy Making](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/strategic-science-communications): Guide on communicating science to policymakers and community leaders.
- [Scientific Councils on Early Childhood Development](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/our-approach/councils): Overview of scientific councils translating research into actionable insights.

## Key Concepts in Child Development

- [Key Concepts in Early Childhood Development](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concepts): Central hub for foundational concepts in early childhood development science.
- [Brain Architecture: An ongoing process that begins before birth](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concepts/brain-architecture): Explains brain construction process from prenatal development through adulthood.
- [Serve and Return: Back-and-forth exchanges](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concepts/serve-and-return): Key concept on responsive caregiver interactions shaping brain architecture.
- [Toxic Stress: What is toxic stress?](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concepts/toxic-stress): Explains toxic stress effects on brain development and lifelong health outcomes.
- [An Expanded Story of Early Childhood Development](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concepts/what-surrounds-us-shapes-us): Explores how environmental experiences shape child development and outcomes.
- [Timing and Critical Periods](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concept/timing-and-critical-periods): Biological sensitivity to adversity during critical developmental periods.
- [Developmental Environments](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concept/developmental-environments): Environmental conditions shaping child development experiences and outcomes.
- [Lifelong Health and Well-being](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concept/lifelong-health): Interconnected biological systems development impacting lifelong health.

## Partnerships and Equity

- [Partnerships and Engagements for Early Childhood Development](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/our-approach/partnerships-engagements): Center's collaborative partnerships driving science-informed policy and practice.
- [Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/our-approach/edib): Center's commitment to equity and confronting systemic racism in early childhood.
